prediction.text:
Bank of America's FY2025 10-K describes several deposit-related liquidity risks. These are unexpected simultaneous draws on deposits, failure to retain deposits (including large-scale migration to digital assets or non-bank platforms), and potential deposit withdrawals modeled in stress scenarios. Uninsured deposits at year-end 2025 were $723.0 billion U.S. and $134.9 billion non-U.S., out of $2.02 trillion in total deposits. The Q2 2026 10-Q says management regards a substantial portion of the deposit base as stable. It also notes that regulatory restrictions limit how liquidity generated by the bank subsidiaries can be used elsewhere in the company.
In its FY2025 10-K risk factors, Bank of America says its liquidity or cost of funds may be negatively impacted by factors including the unwillingness or inability of the Federal Reserve to act as lender of last resort and unexpected simultaneous draws on credit lines or deposits.
The 10-K also lists the failure to attract or retain client deposits or invested funds as a risk, including large-scale deposit migration, such as clients moving balances into digital assets (e.g., stablecoin) or other alternative non-bank financial platforms.
In MD&A, potential deposit withdrawals are listed among the contractual and contingent outflows (alongside increased draws on loan commitments, liquidity facilities and letters of credit). The company notes that changes in market factors, including credit rating downgrades, could negatively impact these potential outflows.
At December 31, 2025, deposits totaled $2.02 trillion, of which estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $723.0 billion and $134.9 billion. Deposits that exceed insurance limits are uninsured.
Bank of America states that its bank subsidiaries' liquidity is primarily driven by deposit and lending activity, as well as securities valuation and net debt activity. It also says it funds a substantial portion of its lending through deposits, which were $2.03 trillion at June 30, 2026.
On the mitigating side, in the Q2 2026 10-Q management says it considers a substantial portion of its deposit base to be a stable, low-cost and consistent source of liquidity. It attributes lower GWIM deposits to an expected seasonal decline from customer tax payments.
Bank of America states that, due to regulatory restrictions, liquidity generated by the bank subsidiaries can generally be used only to fund obligations within the bank subsidiaries, and transfers to the Parent or nonbank subsidiaries may be subject to prior regulatory approval.
The Q2 2026 10-Q refers readers to the Liquidity section of Item 1A Risk Factors in the 2025 10-K for the company's liquidity risks.
